decisions.reason: As a new generation of a core printer technology highlighted on the home page and tightly linked to the firm’s established systems, it is likely performing at or near aspiration and worth retaining under the firm’s R&D-rich, resource-slack conditions.

This software module is a niche extension of the core inline-printing offer, so even if results are somewhat uncertain, its close fit with digitalization and low incremental resource demands support keeping it.

An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces directly extends the firm’s established marking applications, making it a plausible contributor to customer coverage and therefore likely to stay unless performance clearly falls below aspiration.

The mobile decoding app is more peripheral to the firm’s machinery-centered revenue base, and if its contribution has remained uncertain or below aspiration, management would likely reallocate attention and resources to more strategic traceability products.

Inline code verification fits the firm’s move toward serialization and end-to-end traceability, so a large established firm would usually tolerate some uncertainty and keep developing it rather than exit quickly.
Print layout design software complements installed hardware, supports one-stop solutions, and was prominent at launch, so it is likely to be retained as part of the broader system offering.
